61	// truncateRunes returns s capped at max runes plus a trailing ellipsis. It
62	// counts runes, not bytes, so a multi-byte message is never cut mid-rune.
63	func truncateRunes(s string, max int) string {
64		if max < 0 {
65			return ""
66		}
67		runes := []rune(s)
68		if len(runes) <= max {
69			return s
70		}
71		return string(runes[:max]) + "..."
72	}

74	// causePrefix returns a bounded, stable grouping key derived from
75	// Result.Message: the first line, trimmed, capped at causePrefixMaxRunes.
76	// An empty message yields "unknown" so the fingerprint is never empty.
77	func causePrefix(message string) string {
78		line := message
79		if idx := strings.IndexByte(line, '\n'); idx >= 0 {
80			line = line[:idx]
81		}
82		line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
83		if line == "" {
84			return "unknown"
85		}
86		return truncateRunes(line, causePrefixMaxRunes)
87	}

167			Grouping("agent", agentName).
168			Grouping("task_type", a.TaskType).
169			Collector(registry)
170		defer func() {
171			if err := pusher.PushContext(ctx); err != nil {
172				glog.Warningf("prometheus push failed: %v", err)

182		// it usable by every git/gh subprocess. See prepareAuth.
183		resolvedToken, err := a.prepareAuth(ctx)
184		if err != nil {
185			jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
186			jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
187			return err
188		}

190		deliverer := delivery.NewNoopResultDeliverer()
191		if a.TaskID != "" {
192			if len(a.KafkaBrokers) == 0 {
193				jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
194				jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))

202			}
203			defer func() {
204				if err := syncProducer.Close(); err != nil {

251	// finishRun publishes the agent's result and then decides the Job's exit code.
252	// It exists as one call so Run stays within its funlen budget.
253	func finishRun(
254		ctx context.Context,
255		result *agentlib.Result,
256		phase domain.TaskPhase,
257	) error {
258		if err := agentlib.PrintResult(ctx, result); err != nil {
259			return err
260		}
261		return exitErrorForStatus(ctx, result.Status, phase, result.Message)
262	}

264	// exitErrorForStatus returns a non-nil error when the agent's published status
265	// must fail the Job, and nil when the Job may exit 0.
266	//
267	// A failed result is still published to the task, but the Job must also exit
268	// non-zero. The executor records a phase success on exit 0 alone (IsJobSucceeded
269	// in agent-task-executor's job_watcher), so returning nil here makes a failed run
270	// indistinguishable from a completed one: the failure is written as a phase
271	// success, and once the success grace expires the task is parked at human_review
272	// as though a human had parked it deliberately (2026-11-03, task ceb79961: a Job
273	// that published Status=failed for a git clone error exited 0 and parked the
274	// task).
275	//
276	// needs_input is deliberately NOT a failure: parking for a human answer is that
277	// status's intent, and it reaches the same park path on purpose.
278	func exitErrorForStatus(
279		ctx context.Context,
280		status agentlib.AgentStatus,
281		phase domain.TaskPhase,
282		message string,
283	) error {
284		if status != agentlib.AgentStatusFailed {
285			return nil
286		}
287		displayMessage := truncateRunes(message, statusMessageMaxRunes)
288		if displayMessage == "" {
289			displayMessage = "(no message)"
290		}
291		err := errors.Errorf(
292			ctx,
293			"agent reported status %q for phase %q: %s",
294			status,
295			phase,
296			displayMessage,
297		)
298		return &statusError{
299			err: err,
300			fingerprint: []string{
301				"agent-status-failed",
302				string(phase),
303				causePrefix(message),
304			},
305		}
306	}

308	// fingerprinter is implemented by errors that know their Sentry grouping key.
309	type fingerprinter interface {
310		Fingerprint() []string
311	}

313	// statusError is the non-zero-exit error for a failed agent result. The
314	// capture-site stack is identical for every failure, so Sentry would merge
315	// unrelated planning / execution / ai_review causes into one issue; this type
316	// carries an explicit fingerprint (phase + bounded cause prefix) that
317	// sentryFingerprintProcessor installs on the event.
318	type statusError struct {
319		err         error
320		fingerprint []string
321	}
322	
323	func (e *statusError) Error() string { return e.err.Error() }
324	
325	// Unwrap keeps errors.Is / errors.As working through the wrapper.
326	func (e *statusError) Unwrap() error { return e.err }
327	
328	// Cause keeps github.com/bborbe/errors DataFromError traversal working.
329	func (e *statusError) Cause() error { return e.err }

331	// Fingerprint is the Sentry grouping key for this failure.
332	func (e *statusError) Fingerprint() []string { return e.fingerprint }

334	// sentryFingerprintProcessor installs the fingerprint carried by a
335	// fingerprinter error onto the Sentry event. It is a no-op for every other
336	// error, so it can be registered globally: service.Main owns the Sentry client
337	// and exposes no per-client event-processor hook.
338	func sentryFingerprintProcessor(
339		event *sentry.Event,
340		hint *sentry.EventHint,
341	) *sentry.Event {
342		if event == nil || hint == nil || hint.OriginalException == nil {
343			return event
344		}
345		var f fingerprinter
346		if errors.As(hint.OriginalException, &f) {
347			event.Fingerprint = f.Fingerprint()
348		}
349		return event
350	}

378	// prepareAuth resolves the GitHub credential and makes it usable by every
379	// git/gh subprocess: it exports GH_TOKEN (covering the dark-factory daemon,
380	// which inherits os.Environ() for its `git push`) and installs git's credential
381	// helper via `gh auth setup-git`. Returns the resolved token for the
382	// RepoManager / GitHub client / gh-token preflight wiring.
383	func (a *application) prepareAuth(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
384		resolvedToken, err := a.resolveAuth(ctx)
385		if err != nil {
386			return "", err
387		}
388		// resolvedToken is always non-empty here (resolveAuth errors otherwise), but
389		// guard defensively — an empty GH_TOKEN would mislead the daemon subprocess.
390		if resolvedToken != "" {
391			if err := os.Setenv("GH_TOKEN", resolvedToken); err != nil {
392				return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "export GH_TOKEN")
393			}
394		}
395		if err := githubauth.NewGhAuthSetupGit(resolvedToken).Setup(ctx); err != nil {
396			return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "gh auth setup-git")
397		}
398		// A file the daemon re-reads outlives the token bound into gh's helper: the
399		// installation token expires after 60 minutes and the lifecycle daemon keeps
400		// its startup environment, so a long run's own `git fetch` would use a dead
401		// token (2026-11-03, bborbe/trading#433).
402		if err := githubauth.NewFileBackedHelper(resolvedToken).Setup(ctx); err != nil {
403			return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "configure file-backed credential helper")
404		}
405		return resolvedToken, nil
406	}

408	// resolveAuth resolves the GitHub credential forwarded to every git/gh
409	// subprocess. It prefers GitHub App authentication: when APP_ID,
410	// INSTALLATION_ID, and a PEM (file or inline) are all set, it mints a
411	// short-lived installation access token via githubapp.MintIAT. Otherwise it
412	// falls back to the raw GH_TOKEN input — the local cmd/run-task path where the
413	// operator exports `gh auth token`. When neither is configured it returns a
414	// clear error, since the agent cannot clone or push without a credential.
415	//
416	// The token is a runtime value (not a config input), so it is returned to the
417	// caller rather than stored on the argument-parsed application struct —
418	// argument/v2 panics when reflecting over unexported struct fields at startup.
419	func (a *application) resolveAuth(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
420		hasPEMFile := a.PEMKeyFile != ""
421		hasPEMContent := a.PEMKey != ""
422		useGitHubApp := a.AppID != 0 && a.InstallationID != 0 && (hasPEMFile || hasPEMContent)
423		if useGitHubApp {
424			appCfg := githubapp.Config{AppID: a.AppID, InstallationID: a.InstallationID}
425			if hasPEMFile {
426				appCfg.PEMPath = a.PEMKeyFile
427			} else {
428				appCfg.PEM = []byte(a.PEMKey)
429			}
430			// Startup auth must not be killed by the task's work deadline: mint on a
431			// fresh bounded context (keeps ctx values, drops the caller's
432			// deadline/cancel) so a near-deadline task can't fail the token mint.
433			mintCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 30*time.Second)
434			defer cancel()
435			iat, err := githubapp.MintIAT(mintCtx, appCfg)
436			if err != nil {
437				return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "mint github app iat")
438			}
439			glog.V(2).Infof(
440				"github-dark-factory-agent auth mode=github-app app_id=%d installation_id=%d",
441				a.AppID, a.InstallationID,
442			)
443			return iat, nil
444		}
445		if a.GhToken != "" {
446			glog.V(2).Infof("github-dark-factory-agent auth mode=gh-token (raw GH_TOKEN fallback)")
447			return a.GhToken, nil
448		}
449		return "", errors.Errorf(
450			ctx,
451			"github-dark-factory-agent auth: no credentials configured — set GitHub App creds (APP_ID, INSTALLATION_ID, PEM_KEY_FILE or PEM_KEY) or GH_TOKEN",
452		)
453	}

95		}

97			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"] = a.AnthropicBaseURL
98		}
99		if a.AnthropicAuthToken != "" {
100			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN"] = a.AnthropicAuthToken
101		}
102		if a.AnthropicModel != "" {
103			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_MODEL"] = a.AnthropicModel.String()
104		}
105	
106		deliverer := factory.CreateFileResultDeliverer(a.TaskFilePath)
107		repoManager := factory.CreateRepoManager(reposPath, workPath, ghToken)
108		githubClient := factory.CreateGitHubClient(ghToken)
109		claudeProber := factory.CreateClaudeProber(a.ClaudeConfigDir)
110	
111		agent := factory.CreateAgent(
112			a.ClaudeConfigDir,
113			a.AgentDir,
114			a.AnthropicModel,
115			ghToken,
116			claudeEnv,
117			repoManager,
118			githubClient,
119			claudeProber,
120			// Local CLI path: the credential is the operator's own long-lived gh
121			// token, so there is nothing to refresh before the push.
122			nil,

132	// resolveCachePaths fills in defaults for ReposPath/WorkPath when unset
133	// (~/.cache/github-dark-factory-agent/{repos,work}). The pod entry point
134	// requires explicit /repos and /work mounts; local CLI usage benefits from a
135	// default.
136	func (a *application) resolveCachePaths(ctx context.Context) (string, string, error) {
137		reposPath := a.ReposPath
138		workPath := a.WorkPath
139		if reposPath != "" && workPath != "" {
140			return reposPath, workPath, nil
141		}
142		home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
143		if err != nil {
144			return "", "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "resolve user home dir")
145		}
146		if reposPath == "" {
147			reposPath = filepath.Join(home, ".cache", "github-dark-factory-agent", "repos")
148		}
149		if workPath == "" {
150			workPath = filepath.Join(home, ".cache", "github-dark-factory-agent", "work")
151		}
152		return reposPath, workPath, nil
153	}

155	// resolveGhToken returns the configured GhToken, or falls back to `gh auth
156	// token` for ambient local auth. An empty result is returned when neither is
157	// available (the gh-token preflight then escalates cleanly).
158	func (a *application) resolveGhToken(ctx context.Context) string {
159		if a.GhToken != "" {
160			return a.GhToken
161		}
162		// #nosec G204 -- fixed argv; no user-controlled input reaches the command line
163		out, err := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "gh", "auth", "token").Output()
164		if err != nil {
165			glog.V(2).
166				Infof("run-task: `gh auth token` unavailable (%v) — proceeding without a token", err)
167			return ""
168		}
169		return strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
170	}

226	// error, so it can be registered globally: service.Main owns the Sentry client
227	// and exposes no per-client event-processor hook.
228	func sentryFingerprintProcessor(
229		event *sentry.Event,
230		hint *sentry.EventHint,
231	) *sentry.Event {
232		if event == nil || hint == nil || hint.OriginalException == nil {

234		}
235		var f fingerprinter
236		if errors.As(hint.OriginalException, &f) {
237			event.Fingerprint = f.Fingerprint()

Flagging that sibling would abort a healthy multi-spec run 30 s in. `stallGracePolls` 3 → 10 (30 s at the 3 s poll) because `draft`/`approved` have no prompt to watch, so the grace must outlast the daemon's own pickup tick as well as the `prompted` flicker — still turning a 90-minute slot-hold into 30 seconds. The error now names the spec's real status instead of hard-coding `prompted`.

63	- fix: skip the ai_review worktree post-conditions when execution adopted an already-pushed branch. The adopt path routes to ai_review without creating a worktree, but ai_review checked out the task's stale `ref` and demanded every matched spec be completed there — completions the original run had already pushed to the branch, so the check could never pass and every adoption ended in `spec … is not completed (execution did not finish)`. Found on the nuke-dev replay: the run logged `"adopted": true` and then failed one step later. An adopted result now goes straight to the read-only PR verdict; the draft-PR and diff-vs-spec checks still run. Its `## Review` records only those two in `checks_passed` (with `adopted: true`) — not the `specs_completed` / `no_prompts_in_flight` gates the adopted path never evaluates, since that artifact is the human's draft→ready sign-off and must not attest to checks that did not run.

[rejected] HEAD -> <branch> (non-fast-forward)`, leaving a spurious failed task. The execution step now compares the remote branch head with `ref` before `EnsureWorktree`: a head that moved **and** descends from `ref` is adopted (no lifecycle, `## Result` written citing the head with `adopted: true` and `prompts_executed: 0`); a head that moved but does not descend from `ref` returns needs-input naming both shas rather than claiming another push's work.

79	- fix: **`waitForDrain` fails fast when a requested spec is stranded at `prompted` with no prompt referencing it**, instead of holding the Job's only agent slot until the lifecycle deadline. ⚠️ dark-factory advances a spec out of `prompted` only through its spec-link scan (`CheckAndComplete`), which no-ops when no prompt carries `spec:` — so a prompt authored without the link leaves the spec unreachable and every later daemon tick a no-op. `drained()` cannot see this: it counts in-flight prompts, and a stranded run has none. 91	- fix: **Go 1.27.2 now passes `make precommit`.** The standalone `errcheck:` and `gosec:` targets are both retired and dropped from `check:`, and both linters now run embedded in golangci-lint, which `.golangci.yml` already enabled. `GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION` moves v2.13.1 → v2.14.0, the `go` directive and `Dockerfile` move to 1.27.2, and `golang.org/x/net` moves v0.58.0 → v0.60.0. ⚠️ **Neither target was repairable, which is why both are removed rather than repointed.** `go run github.com/kisielk/errcheck@v1.20.0` and `go run github.com/securego/gosec/v2/cmd/gosec@$(GOSEC_VERSION)` each build in their **own** module context, pinning a `golang.org/x/tools` reader that stops at export-data version 4 while the 1.27.2 toolchain emits version 5, so each dies with `internal error: package "X" without types was imported` at any `go.mod` directive. Dropping the `@$(ERRCHECK_VERSION)` pin does not rescue it either: `precommit` runs `ensure` → `go mod tidy` first, and tidy strips a require nothing imports. ⚠️ **Coverage is preserved, not traded away.** `.golangci.yml` gains `settings.errcheck.exclude-functions` carrying the retired target's `-ignore '(Close|Write|Fprint)'` list, and `settings.gosec.excludes: [G104]` carrying `-exclude=G104`. The `go` directive bump is load-bearing rather than tidy: it is what clears the nine `stdlib@v1.27.1 -> v1.27.2` advisories that `osv-scanner` reports, and it could not move while the standalone targets ran. Also bumps `osv-scanner` v2.3.1 → v2.6.0: the pinned v2.3.1 panics during call-graph analysis in `golang.org/x/tools@v0.38.0/go/ssa`, and v2.6.0 carries a fixed x/tools.

130	- fix: fail-fast on a permanently-failed prompt instead of hanging to the lifecycle deadline. When a dark-factory prompt exhausts its retries the failure handler leaves it in `prompts/in-progress` with `status: failed` and the scanner skips it forever ("queue blocked until manual retry"), so its spec can never reach `verifying`. `drained()` could not distinguish that dead prompt from a slow one, so `waitForDrain` spun until the 30-minute `lifecycleTimeout` — and in-cluster the overall-run budget hard-killed the Job with `context canceled` at ~30 min BEFORE the step could escalate, so no `## Failure` was ever written and the task was not cleanly parked. `waitForDrain` now scans `prompts/in-progress` each tick via new `findFailedPrompt` and returns a lifecycle error the moment a prompt reaches terminal `status: failed`, surfacing its `lastFailReason`. The execution step then escalates cleanly (`Status: failed`) within seconds while the context is still alive — PR stays draft, spec stays incomplete, task parks. Approved/executing/unparseable prompts are ignored (only terminal `failed` counts). Unit tests cover the detector's discrimination + the RunLifecycle fast-path timing.

132	## v0.3.9
133	
134	- fix: commit the spec-completion move before pushing, so completed specs actually reach the PR branch. `dark-factory spec complete` (which the execution step drives after the daemon stops) rewrites the working tree — moving the spec `specs/in-progress → specs/completed` — but does NOT git-commit it (nothing commits it once the daemon is gone, unlike the daemon's per-prompt `workflow:direct` commits). `PushBranch` is a bare `git push HEAD`, so the completion was silently dropped: the PR kept an approved-not-completed spec, the watcher re-emitted the task on the agent's own push, and runs overlapped indefinitely (self-trigger loop). New `ExecutionRunner.CommitSpecChanges` stages `specs/` and commits after `completeSpecs` and before `PushBranch` (no-op when nothing is staged). Now the completed spec lands on the branch → the watcher stops re-triggering → clean multi-spec drain to `human_review`. Unit tests cover the commit + the no-op path and assert the execution step calls it before pushing.

136	## v0.3.8
137	
138	- fix: `RunLifecycle` no longer stops the dark-factory daemon while a generated prompt is still awaiting auto-approval. The drain check (`drained()`) only looked at `prompts/in-progress`, ignoring the generation **inbox** (`prompts/*.md` at the repo root, where a freshly generated prompt waits for the daemon's auto-approve audit). Because the daemon flips the spec to `verifying` while that audit runs, `drained()` returned true mid-audit, `stopDaemon` SIGKILLed the in-flight audit subprocess (`auto-approve: audit FAILED ... signal: killed`), the prompt was never approved/executed, and the implementation file (e.g. the `HELLO_DARK_FACTORY.md` marker) was never created — ai_review then correctly escalated on the absent file. New `hasInboxPrompts` gates the drain on the inbox too, so the lifecycle waits for the prompt to be approved → executed → completed. Surfaced on go-skeleton PR #40 (master `.dark-factory.yaml` sets `validationPrompt: docs/dod.md`, making the audit slow enough to lose the race). Unit test drives a stub daemon that leaves a prompt in the inbox and asserts the lifecycle does not drain.

141	
142	- fix: inject the fleet model into the backend:local daemon. The execution step now forwards the configured model (`claudelib.ClaudeModel`, from the pod's `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`) to `dark-factory daemon` as `--set model=<model>` via `NewExecutionStep`'s new constructor arg — no `os.Getenv` inside the step. The daemon resolves its model from `--set` > `.dark-factory.yaml` `model:` > a built-in Claude default; because it does NOT read `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` for its own selection, a target repo whose `.dark-factory.yaml` omits `model:` silently ran on Sonnet (a ToU violation), which on go-skeleton PR #40 produced a prompt asserting the wrong byte count and never committed the marker. Injecting the model makes the fleet model authoritative regardless of per-repo config. Unit test asserts the flag is forwarded.

146	- fix: ai_review no longer flags dark-factory's own bookkeeping as out-of-scope. Previously a correct implementation escalated to `failed` at ai_review because a spec constraint like "No other file is modified" can never hold for this pipeline (observed in cluster E2E: the marker was created correctly but the reviewer flagged the prompt/spec churn). The reviewer now judges only real implementation files against the spec. Verified via the local `cmd/run-task` loop against a clean draft PR: the same scenario now returns `pass` → `human_review`.

148	- chore: bump `golang.org/x/text` v0.38.0 → v0.39.0 (indirect) — clears CVE-2026-56852 (infinite loop on invalid input) flagged by trivy.

152	- chore: bump baked `DARK_FACTORY_VERSION` v0.192.0 → v0.192.4 (CLI + plugin). v0.192.4 fixes the `generate-prompts-for-spec` command's hardcoded `/workspace` paths (docker-mount convention) → cwd-relative, so backend:local generation writes prompts into the worktree the daemon watches instead of an empty `/workspace`. Unblocks the backend:local generation→execution lifecycle.

155	
156	- fix: populate remote-tracking refs (`refs/remotes/origin/*`) in the RepoManager's bare clone. `git clone --bare` maps remote branches to `refs/heads/*`, so `origin/master` never resolved in a worktree — and dark-factory's per-prompt "sync with default branch" (`git merge origin/<default>`, run by every workflow) failed with `origin/master - not something we can merge`, stalling execution after generation. New `configureRemoteTracking` sets the standard `+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*` refspec and fetches, on both the clone and update paths.

159	
160	- fix: bake the `coding` plugin into the runtime image (Dockerfile), alongside the existing `dark-factory` plugin. dark-factory's generation step invokes the prompt-creator agent, which uses the `coding` plugin's Go guides to write prompt files; without it the fleet's MiniMax model (`MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`) produced no prompt file ("generation produced no prompt files") and the spec never left `approved`. 163	
164	- fix: stream the `dark-factory` daemon's stdout/stderr to the agent's own stdout in `dark_factory_runner.startDaemon` (was `cmd.Stdout/Stderr = nil`, i.e. discarded). The backend:local lifecycle — and the claude subprocesses the daemon spawns — is now visible in `kubectl logs`. Without it a hung daemon (e.g. a claude call blocking on a no-TTY onboarding prompt) was indistinguishable from slow progress until the 30-minute lifecycle deadline. Writes to the process stdout/stderr, not a repo file, so it is not swept into the daemon's commits.

167	
168	- fix: hoist `ARG CLAUDE_YOLO_IMAGE` to global scope (before the first `FROM`) in the Dockerfile. It was declared inside the build stage, so the runtime `FROM ${CLAUDE_YOLO_IMAGE}` could not interpolate it and BuildKit aborted with "base name should not be blank" — `make buca` failed before any push. CI runs `make precommit` (go build/test/lint), never `docker build`, so this latent bug surfaced only on the first real image build.
169	- fix: build the dark-factory CLI from the pinned clone (`go install .` in the module root) instead of `go install github.com/bborbe/dark-factory@${DARK_FACTORY_VERSION}`. dark-factory's `go.mod` carries `exclude` directives, which `go install pkg@version` refuses; building from the module root honors them (same as upstream `make install`). Reuses the clone the runtime image already makes for the plugin marketplace, so there is now a single pinned clone for both CLI and plugin. Both fixes verified with a local `make build`.

171	## v0.3.0
172	
173	- feat: add GitHub App authentication. When `APP_ID`, `INSTALLATION_ID`, and a PEM (`PEM_KEY_FILE` or `PEM_KEY`) are all set, the agent mints a short-lived installation access token at startup (`githubapp.MintIAT`) and forwards it to every git/gh subprocess — `os.Setenv("GH_TOKEN", …)` covers the dark-factory daemon's `git push` (inherits `os.Environ()`), `gh auth setup-git` installs the git credential helper, and the token is threaded into the RepoManager, GitHub REST client, and gh-token preflight. Fixes cluster clone/push failures where the pod set no `GH_TOKEN`. Copies `pkg/githubauth` (the `gh auth setup-git` configurator) from github-pr-review-agent.

Validated in the local E2E: the daemon now starts and runs inside the worktree.
176	- fix: install the dark-factory Claude PLUGIN in the runtime image (Dockerfile), not just the CLI binary. The backend:local lifecycle runs `/dark-factory:generate-prompts-for-spec` and `/dark-factory:audit-prompt` *inside* claude; with only the CLI installed, claude reports `Unknown command` → zero prompts generated → the spec silently resets to `approved` and the daemon idles (the E2E root cause, 2026-07-13). Confirmed locally: with the plugin installed, generation produces a valid prompt.
177	- docs: record two backend:local provisioning requirements in design.md Part 5 — (1) the dark-factory plugin must be installed in the runtime `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`; (2) backend:local ignores dark-factory `config.env`, so the model-router `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` + auth token must be pod env vars (a spec-104 follow-up gap).

179	## v0.2.0
180	
181	- feat: implement Increment 1 of the three-phase implementer — wire planning/execution/ai_review as distinct phases (domain.TaskPhase constants), route the `dark-factory-implement` task type; add RepoManager (bare-clone cache + per-task worktree), claude-auth + gh-token preflight steps, and the pure-Go planning step (clone + precondition scan: ref==PR head, PR draft, `.dark-factory.yaml` present, approved-not-completed spec in the PR diff → writes `## Plan`, routes execution; escalates without mutating assignee/status); wire `cmd/run-task` as a local per-phase harness. Execution/ai_review are stubs (Increments 2/3).

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## Unreleased

- fix: **carry the failed result's message into the non-zero-exit error and fingerprint the Sentry event by phase + cause prefix.** `exitErrorForStatus` built its error from status and phase only, so every failed run produced the same capture-site stack and Sentry merged unrelated planning / execution / ai_review causes into one umbrella issue (`NUKE-PROD-CV`). include tools.env

default: precommit

precommit: ensure format generate shellcheck test check addlicense
	@echo "ready to commit"

# The cluster-build scripts under hack/ handle credentials (teamvault → Secret)
# and run as root inside a Job, so they get a lint pass. `-S warning` keeps it to
# real defects: the SC1091 infos are dynamic `source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/…"` paths
# shellcheck cannot resolve, and they are present in every repo that vendors this
# set. shellcheck ships on GitHub's ubuntu-latest runners, so CI needs no install.
.PHONY: shellcheck
shellcheck:
	shellcheck -S warning hack/*.sh

ensure:
	go mod tidy
	go mod verify
	rm -rf vendor

format:
	find . -type f -name 'go.mod' -not -path './vendor/*' -exec go run github.com/shoenig/go-modtool@$(GO_MODTOOL_VERSION) -w fmt "{}" \;
	go run github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/v3@$(GOIMPORTS_REVISER_VERSION) -project-name github.com/bborbe/github-dark-factory-agent -format -excludes vendor ./...
	find . -type d -name vendor -prune -o -type f -name '*.go' -print0 | xargs -0 -n 10 go run github.com/segmentio/golines@$(GOLINES_VERSION) --max-len=100 -w
	find . -type f -name '*.go' -not -path './vendor/*' -exec gofmt -w "{}" +

generate:
	rm -rf mocks avro
	mkdir -p mocks
	echo "package mocks" > mocks/mocks.go
	go generate -mod=mod ./...

.PHONY: generatek8s
generatek8s:
	bash hack/update-codegen.sh

# -race=true catches data races but flakes on some CI runners (rare SIGSEGV
# during gexec.Build in cmd/*-style binary smoke tests). Default off; opt in
# via ENABLE_RACE=true for nightly/manual hardening runs.
TESTFLAGS_RACE = -race=false
ifdef ENABLE_RACE
	TESTFLAGS_RACE = -race=true
endif

.PHONY: test
test:
	go test -mod=mod -p=$${GO_TEST_PARALLEL:-1} -cover $(TESTFLAGS_RACE) $(shell go list -mod=mod ./... | grep -v /vendor/)

check: lint vet vulncheck osv-scanner trivy

lint:
	go run github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@$(GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION) run --allow-parallel-runners --config .golangci.yml ./...

vet:
	go vet -mod=mod $(shell go list -mod=mod ./... | grep -v /vendor/)

# errcheck is no longer run standalone. `go run github.com/kisielk/errcheck@v1.20.0`
# builds in errcheck's OWN module context, which pins golang.org/x/tools v0.44.0 — a
# reader that stops at export data version 4, while the Go 1.27.2 toolchain emits
# version 5. The target therefore dies with `internal error: package "context" without
# types was imported`, on every repo, at any go.mod directive. It is NOT repairable by
# editing this repo's graph: `ensure` runs `go mod tidy` first, and tidy strips a require
# nothing imports. errcheck is embedded in golangci-lint instead (see .golangci.yml →
# settings.errcheck, which carries the equivalent exclude-functions for the old
# `-ignore '(Close|Write|Fprint)'` flag).

VULNCHECK_IGNORE ?= GO-2026-4923 GO-2026-4514 GO-2022-0470 GO-2026-4772 GO-2026-4771 GO-2026-5932 GO-2026-4970 GO-2026-5856

.PHONY: vulncheck
vulncheck:
	@PKGS="$(shell go list -mod=mod ./... | grep -v /vendor/)"; \
	IGNORE_JSON=$$(printf '%s\n' $(VULNCHECK_IGNORE) | jq -R . | jq -s .); \
	REMAIN=$$(go run golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@$(GOVULNCHECK_VERSION) -format json $$PKGS 2>/dev/null | \
		jq -rs --argjson ignore "$$IGNORE_JSON" \
			'(map(select(.osv != null)) | map({key: .osv.id, value: (.osv.summary // "")}) | from_entries) as $$sum | \
			 map(select(.finding != null) | .finding) | \
			 map(select(.osv as $$o | $$ignore | index($$o) | not)) | \
			 map("\(.osv)\t\(.trace[-1].module)@\(.trace[-1].version) -> \(.fixed_version)\t\($$sum[.osv] // "")") | \
			 unique | .[]'); \
	if [ -n "$$REMAIN" ]; then \
		echo "Unexpected vulnerabilities (ignored: $(VULNCHECK_IGNORE)):"; \
		printf '%s\n' "$$REMAIN" | column -t -s "$$(printf '\t')"; \
		exit 1; \
	else \
		echo "No unignored vulnerabilities found"; \
	fi

osv-scanner:
	@if [ -f .osv-scanner.toml ]; then \
		echo "Using .osv-scanner.toml"; \
		go run github.com/google/osv-scanner/v2/cmd/osv-scanner@$(OSV_SCANNER_VERSION) --config .osv-scanner.toml --recursive .; \
	else \
		echo "No config found, running default scan"; \
		go run github.com/google/osv-scanner/v2/cmd/osv-scanner@$(OSV_SCANNER_VERSION) --recursive .; \
	fi

# gosec is no longer run standalone, for the same reason as errcheck above: `gosec@$(GOSEC_VERSION)`
# also builds in its own module context and dies at Go 1.27.2 with `internal error: package
# "X" without types was imported`. It is embedded in golangci-lint instead (see .golangci.yml →
# settings.gosec, which carries the equivalent `excludes: [G104]` for the old `-exclude=G104`).

.PHONY: trivy
trivy:
	trivy fs \
	--db-repository ghcr.io/aquasecurity/trivy-db \
	$(if $(wildcard .trivyignore),--ignorefile .trivyignore,$(if $(wildcard $(ROOTDIR)/.trivyignore),--ignorefile $(ROOTDIR)/.trivyignore,)) \
	$(if $(wildcard .trivy-secret.yaml),--secret-config .trivy-secret.yaml,$(if $(wildcard $(ROOTDIR)/.trivy-secret.yaml),--secret-config $(ROOTDIR)/.trivy-secret.yaml,)) \
	--scanners vuln,secret \
	--skip-dirs vendor \
	--quiet \
	--no-progress \
	--disable-telemetry \
	--exit-code 1 .

addlicense:
	go run github.com/google/addlicense@$(ADDLICENSE_VERSION) -c "Benjamin Borbe" -y $$(date +'%Y') -l bsd $$(find . -name "*.go" -not -path './vendor/*')
